doc.title: Michael Weiss interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 22, 2021

title: Need for work and the sports analogy
summary: Rowe hopes Weiss will mentor others as he did with Griffin; Weiss says musicians need to play constantly, using a baseball analogy.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Advice to young musicians starting out

blocks.x: Yeah, that’s a good observation. Well this has really been a fascinating conversation and I congratulate you on your career so far. And I hope that you will be thought of as one of those people like when you apprenticed with Johnny Griffin that people will be doing that with you.
You know all we need right now is just work. Like I talked about before, we need, the jazz musician needs to play. You just can’t develop as an artist unless you’re able to do it all the time.

Another sports analogy, you know like a baseball season is 162 games. That’s like six games a week for six months. So, and even with that, a great batting average is like three out of ten times you get a hit. Imagine if you just play one game a week, what’s your average going to be then?
